texts.facts: The petitioner while invoking the inherent power of this Court saved under Section 482, Cr.PC has sought quashing of the compliant, titled as "Drug Inspector, Kathua V/s M/s Cheap Medical Store and Ors" (for short, the impugned complaint) pending before the Court of Chief Judicial Magistrate, Kathua (for short the trial court) proceedings initiated therein alongwith order dated 27.08.2013 as also the order of revisional Court dated 06.01.2016. 2. It has been alleged in the impugned complaint that a drug namely, Sneeze Go Suspension' manufactured by M/s Zee Laboratories Ltd. C/w and distributed by the proforma respondents 2 and 3 herein, was found to be sub-standard upon analysis by the Government Analyst, constituting thus the offences covered in the complainant under the Act of 1940 and as the petitioner herein is being the authorized signatory of said M/s Zee Laboratories Ltd and responsible for managing the affairs of said M/s Zee Laboratories Ltd, was also found involved in the commissions of offences in question. on 16 December, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/156935387/ 1 accused persons including the petitioner herein, feeling aggrieved whereof, the petitioner herein challenged the maintainability of the compliant including the proceedings initiated thereon as well as the order of cognizance dated 27.08.2013 in a revision petition before the Court Additional Sessions Judge, Kathua, which revision petition, however came to be dismissed in terms of order dated 06.01.2016, as consequences whereof, the petitioner herein has maintained the instant petition calling in question not only the impugned complaint, proceedings initiated thereon, the order of cognizance dated 27.08.2013 as well the order of dismissal passed by the revisional Court dated 06.01.2016. 4. The petitioner in the instant petition, while invoking the inherent power of this Court saved under Section 482, Cr.PC has sought quashing of the proceedings in case No. 04/complaint titled as "Drug Inspector, Kathua C/w V/s M/s Cheap Medical Store and Ors" (for short, the impugned complaint) pending before the Court of Chief Judicial Magistrate, Kathua (for short the trial court), the proceedings initiated therein alongwith order dated 09.10.2014 as also the order passed by the Revisional Court dated 06.01.2016 titled as "Dhananjay Kumar Sharma vs. Drugs Inspector Kathua". 5. The petitioner herein claims to be the authorized signatory of Drug Manufacturing Company namely, M/s Zee Laboratories ltd. having its registered office at 913, D-Mall Neta ji Subash Place, Pitampura, Delhi possessed of a licence under the Drugs and Cosmetics Act, 1940 for manufacturing, sale and distribution of the drugs. 6. The respondent 1 herein is stated to have filed a criminal complaint against the petitioner herein before the trial court alleging therein the commission of offence under Section 18(a)(i) read with Section 27 of the Drug and Cosmetic Act, 1940, impleading proforma respondents 2 and 3 therein in the said complaint as accused 1 and 2 and the petitioner herein as accused 3 while complaining that a drug namely, "Aceflex-P Suspension" upon analysis by the Government Analyst, was found to be not of standard quality. 7. Upon entertaining the complaint, the trial court is stated to have taken cognizance of the offence alleged against the petitioner herein and other accused persons in terms of impugned order dated 09.10.2014 and consequently summoned the accused persons including the petitioner herein, aggrieved whereof the petitioner herein filed a revision petition C/w before the Revisional Court, which revision petition however, came to be dismissed by the Revisional Court in terms of order dated 06.01.2016. 8. The instant petitions have been maintained by the petitioner on the following grounds:- i.

It is submitted that on the plain reading section 34 of the Drugs and Cosmetics Act, 1940, "if a person who commits an offence under the Act is a company, the company as well as every person in charge of and responsible to the company for the conduct of business of the company at time of commission of offence is deemed to be guilty of the offence". There is well settled law laid down by Hon'ble Supreme Court in Aneeta Hada V/s Godfather Travels & Tours Ltd. 2012 (5) SCC 661 that commission of an offence by the company / firm is an express condition precedent to attract the vicarious liability of other persons / directors and the words "as well as the company" appearing in the section 34 make it absolutely and unmistakably clear that when the company / firm is prosecuted, then only the persons mentioned in other categories could be vicariously liable for the offence subject to the averments in the petition and prove thereof, thus, for maintaining the prosecution under section 34 of the Act against partners, arraigning of a company / firm as an accused is imperative. iv. According to Mr. Varut Gupta appearing counsel for the petitioner, the impugned complaint was not liable to be entertained by the trial Court, in that, the complainant respondent herein did not array the Manufacturing Company, namely, M/s Zee Laboratories Ltd as an accused therein the complaints and instead impleaded the petitioner herein alone being its authorized signatory, in breach and violation of the mandate of Section 34 of the Act of 1940 and that both the courts below over looked the mandate of the said Section 34 of the Act of 1940 and in the process, grossly erred or in law. According to Mr. Gupta, Section 34 of Act of 1940 is pari materia with Section 141 of Negotiable Instrument Act, 1881 and the Apex Court while interpreting the provisions of Section of 141 of the said Act has ruled that for maintaining a prosecution under the said Act of 1881 against a company for an offence committed by such company, arraying of the company as an accused is imperative and that the other offenders connected with such company can only be implicated on the touch stone of vicarious liability. Mr. Gupta in support of his aforesaid submissions would heavily rely upon the judgments of the Apex Court passed in case titled as Aneeta Hada vs. Godfather Travel and Tours Private ltd. C/w reported in (2012) 5 SCC 661 and Dilip Hariramani vs. Bank of Baroda, reported in AIR 2022 (SC) 2258. According to Mr. Gupta, in view of the law lay down by the Apex Court in case titled as Dilip Hariramani supra, in absence of arraignment of the Company/Principal accused in compliant under the Act of 1940, a person connected with the affairs of the Company, such Company cannot alone be arrayed as an accused and such defect in such a complaint would vitiate the compliant ab initio in law. 11.
